free_tier.stated: Public images are free up to 75 GB of storage; private images are €0.027/GB/month: 'Public images | Free up to 75GB | ... | Free'. The FAQ repeats it verbatim with dated validation ('validation: 2025-08-19').
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: The registry's own table only covers Scaleway-to-Scaleway traffic: 'Public images | Free up to 75GB | Inter-regional: free - Intra-regional: free', where 'Inter-regional traffic: AMS ↔ PAR, WAW ↔ PAR, or AMS ↔ WAW' and 'Intra-regional traffic: PAR ↔ PAR ..'. EXTERNAL internet egress is simply not mentioned anywhere on the registry FAQ or the containers pricing page. That silence is the finding, not a free grant. Scaleway's account-wide bandwidth meter elsewhere reads 'Egress fees* | 75 GB free every month, then €0.01/GB', with 'Egress fees include external outgoing data transfer and inter-region data transfers'. So the '75 GB free' headline is an Object Storage/everything-else allowance; applying it to registry pulls is an inference, not a quote. Treat registry internet egress as metered-at-€0.01/GB beyond 75 GB/month. Cheap, still a per-GB meter, therefore a fail.

tooling: docker/skopeo/ORAS; scw CLI. Registry is Harbor-based.
chaining: 75 GB public storage per namespace x N Scaleway accounts/projects; the egress allowance is per account, not per namespace, so egress does not multiply the same way.
limits_note: 75 GB free public-image storage per account; egress 75 GB/month free then €0.01/GB; private images €0.027/GB/month; unlimited versions supported.
reliability_note: Clean and fast EU-hosted service; the egress meter is the failure mode, not reliability.
confidence_note: Unverified: carried from historical research records without live verification. A first-party page read confirms documentation.
